url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS:

| Method | What you’ll run | Why it’s useful |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Quick, scriptable, works from any terminal that has the Cloud SDK installed. |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` | Useful if you’re building a custom integration or want to call the API directly from code. |

---

## 1. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., us-central1-b)
ZONE="us-central1-b"

# 2️⃣  Pick a machine type that can host the GPU (e.g., n1-standard-8)
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"

# 3️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --guest-os-features=VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE,VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE \
  --service-account=$(gcloud iam service-accounts list --filter="displayName:default" --format="value(email)") \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --labels=environment=dev,team=ai
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Zone that supports GPUs. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory capacity. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional startup script to install GPU drivers automatically. |
| `--service-account` | Uses the default Compute Engine service account. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. |
| `--labels` | Adds metadata tags for cost allocation, etc. |

> **Tip:**  
> *If you want the GPU driver installed automatically, create a `startup.sh` script that runs the NVIDIA driver installer. The Cloud SDK will upload it as metadata.*

---

## 2. Using the REST API

Below is a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine API. Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your own values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default@{project}.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "environment": "dev",
    "team": "ai"
  }
}
```

### How to call it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/us-central1-b/instances"
```

> **Note:**  
> *Make sure the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator type is available in the chosen zone. You can list available types with:*
> ```bash
> gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=us-central1-b
> ```

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Billing enabled for the project |
| ✅ | GPU API enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| ✅ | Zone supports GPUs (`gcloud compute zones describe us-central1-b`) |
| ✅ | Machine type can host the GPU (`gcloud compute machine-types describe n1-standard-8`) |
| ✅ | GPU driver installed (via startup script or manually) |
| ✅ | Firewall rules allow SSH/HTTP/HTTPS if needed |

---

### Final Thoughts

* **gcloud CLI** is great for quick one‑off commands or CI pipelines.  
* **REST API** gives you fine‑grained control and is ideal for custom tooling.  

Both approaches will give you a running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU ready for your workloads.
